source.title: A Practical Approach to Sizing Neural Networks
source.authors: G. Friedland; M. Krell; A. Metere

record.tranche_reason: Uses random points and labelings as a capacity-estimation method and treats memorization as a worst-case generalization case, but reports no results testing the listed random-label or random-input claims.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. for randomization findings; those cited results are not this study's. Its own table reports validation accuracy for capacity estimates on named datasets, not results for the listed claim versions. The ImageNet passage also reports separate accuracy values at smaller capacities.
record.test_reason: The study uses memorization of random points and binary labelings to measure network capacity. Its reported capacity curves and dataset-sizing experiments do not establish any listed version: they do not compare standard deep networks on true versus random labels under unchanged training settings, test the specified input randomizations, or measure learning order. Zhang and Arpit supply the cited randomization findings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors propose information-theoretic capacity bounds and claim their heuristic estimates are close to experimentally required capacities. They recommend sizing initially for memorization and then reducing parameters to improve generalization and explainability; those improvements are recommendations and expectations, not demonstrated outcomes here.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a capacity model and heuristic estimator, with experiments on named datasets; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: For the ImageNet subset, reported accuracy changes with network capacity: 94.6% at 5 kbit, 97.3% at 9 kbit, 97.9% at 11 kbit, and 98.2% at 10253 bits.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks at the listed capacities achieve the reported accuracies on structured binary tasks and a two-class ImageNet subset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The heuristic capacity estimates approximately match capacities yielding high classification accuracy on these selected datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: The capacity-measurement section reports implementation-dependent effectiveness, practical linear capacity scaling, and predicted behavior for sigmoid and ReLU, using random points and possible binary labelings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-point memorization can benchmark implementation-specific storage capacity against the authors' proposed bounds.

record.problems: The authors describe image experiments as anecdotal and identify initialization, learning rate, regularization, and other factors as affecting accuracy. Uncertainty estimates are not reported for the table results.

untested.parts: Random-label training and chance test error in standard deep networks with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 3 and the capacity-measurement discussion contain relevant background beyond Table 1, but measure shattering capacity rather than a listed version. The record's claim that ImageNet accuracy increases across all reported capacities needs correction because the reported 11-kbit result conflicts with that ordering.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random training labels, with test error at chance and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random versus true labels and convergence as corruption grows.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep from no corrupted labels to all corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.operation_detail: Validation experiment for the capacity estimate on AND, 2 variables.
rows.note: The paper does not state the network architecture for this row; the size is the capacity shown in the table. This is not a random-label result.
rows.check: The architecture is stated: one perceptron without bias. The 2-bit capacity and 100% accuracy validate the sizing heuristic on AND, not random-label fitting.

rows.subject: 3-layer neural network
rows.operation_detail: Validation experiment for the capacity estimate on a selected ImageNet subset.

conditions.value: ImageNet: 2000 images in 2 classes (“hummingbird” and “snow leopard”)

rows.note: The images were JPEG-compressed at quality 20 and converted to grayscale. Authors call such image experiments anecdotal and name initialization, learning rate, and regularization among factors affecting accuracy. This is not a random-label result.
rows.check: Images retain their class labels. The table calls this validation accuracy, while the accompanying text describes memorization; a held-out evaluation is not specified. The 10253-bit capacity was selected by successively increasing capacity.
